context.title: David's Royal Line
context.summary: This chapter lists David's sons, the kings of Judah from Solomon to Josiah, and then David's descendants through the exile and beyond, including Zerubbabel.
context.background: David reigned seven and a half years in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem (v. 4). The list carries David's family several generations past Zerubbabel, the governor who led the first return; this is one clue for dating Chronicles. Here Zerubbabel is a son of Pedaiah (v. 19), while Ezra 3:2 calls him son of Shealtiel.

customs.note: Another name for King Jehoiachin, taken to Babylon in 597 BC. 'Assir' in v. 17 may be a name or may mean 'the captive.'

watchFor: An unbroken line of kings, father to son (vv. 10–16).
The royal family survives the exile — the promise to David is not dead (vv. 17–24).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Amnon
people.summary: The eldest son of David, by Ahinoam of Jezreel (1 Chr. 3:1; 2 Sam. 3:2).

people.name: Abigail
people.summary: The wife of the churlish Nabal, who dwelt in the district of Carmel (1 Sam. 25:3). She showed great prudence and delicate management at a critical period of her husband’s life.

people.name: Ahinoam
people.summary: A Jezreelitess, the first wife of David (1 Sam. 25:43; 27:3). She was the mother of Amnon (2 Sam. 3:2).

people.name: Daniel
people.summary: David’s second son, “born unto him in Hebron, of Abigail the Carmelitess” (1 Chr. 3:1).

people.name: Absalom
people.summary: Father of peace; i.e., “peaceful” David’s son by Maacah (2 Sam. 3:3; comp. 1 Kings 1:6). He was noted for his personal beauty and for the extra-ordinary profusion of the hair of his head (2 Sam. 14:25,26).

people.name: Adonijah
people.summary: The fourth son of David (2 Sam. 3:4). After the death of his elder brothers, Amnon and Absalom, he became heir-apparent to the throne. But Solomon, a younger brother, was preferred to him.

people.name: Haggith
people.summary: Festive; the dancer, a wife of David and the mother of Adonijah (2 Sam. 3:4; 1 Kings 1:5, 11; 2:13; 1 Chr. 3:2), who, like Absalom, was famed for his beauty.

people.name: Talmai
people.summary: A king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after he had put Amnon to death (2 Sam. 3:3; 13:37).

people.name: Maacah
people.summary: A daughter of Talmai, king of the old native population of Geshur.

people.name: Abital
people.summary: Father of dew; i.e., “fresh”, David’s fifth wife (2 Sam. 3:4).

people.name: Eglah
people.summary: A heifer, one of David’s wives, and mother of Ithream (2 Sam. 3:5; 1 Chr. 3:3).

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Bathsheba
people.summary: Daughter of the oath, or of seven, called also Bath-shu’a (1 Chr. 3:5), was the daughter of Eliam (2 Sam. 11:3) or Ammiel (1 Chr. 3:5), and wife of Uriah the Hittite.

people.name: Nathan
people.summary: A son of David, by Bathsheba (2 Sam. 5:14), whose name appears in the genealogy of Mary, the mother of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

people.name: Shammua
people.summary: One of David’s sons by Bathsheba (1 Chr. 3:5); called also Shammua (14:4).

people.name: Shobab
people.summary: One of David’s sons by Bathseheba (2 Sam. 5:14).

people.name: Eliam
people.summary: The father of Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah (2 Sam. 11:3).

people.name: Elishua
people.summary: God his salvation, a son of David, 2 Sam. 5:15 = Elishama, 1 Chr. 3:6.

people.name: Ibhar
people.summary: Chosen, one of David’s sons (1 Chr. 3:6; 2 Sam. 5:15).

people.name: Japhia
people.summary: One of the sons of David (2 Sam. 5:15), born in Jerusalem.

people.name: Nepheg
people.summary: Weak.

people.name: Nogah
people.summary: Splendour, one of David’s sons, born at Jerusalem (1 Chr. 3:7).

people.name: Eliada
people.summary: One of David’s sons born after his establishment in Jerusalem (2 Sam. 5:16).

people.name: Eliphalet
people.summary: God his deliverance, one of David’s sons (2 Sam. 5:16); called also Eliphelet (1 Chr. 3:8).

people.name: Tamar
people.summary: A daughter of David (2 Sam. 13:1-32; 1 Chr. 3:9), whom Amnon shamefully outraged and afterwards “hated exceedingly,” thereby illustrating the law of human nature noticed even by the heathen, “Proprium humani ingenii est odisse quem laeseris”, i.e., “It is the property of human nature to hate one whom you have injured.”

people.name: Jehoshaphat
people.summary: The son and successor of Asa, king of Judah. After fortifying his kingdom against Israel (2 Chr. 17:1, 2), he set himself to cleanse the land of idolatry (1 Kings 22:43).

people.name: Asa
people.summary: Physician, son of Abijah and grandson of Rehoboam, was the third king of Judah. He was zealous in maintaining the true worship of God, and in rooting all idolatry, with its accompanying immoralities, out of the land (1 Kings 15:8-14).

people.name: Rehoboam
people.summary: He enlarges the people, the successor of Solomon on the throne, and apparently his only son. He was the son of Naamah “the Ammonitess,” some well-known Ammonitish princess (1 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 12:13).

people.name: Abijah
people.summary: The son of Rehoboam, whom he succeeded on the throne of Judah (1 Chr. 3:10). He is also called Abijam (1 Kings 14:31; 15:1-8). He began his three years’ reign (2 Chr. 12:16; 13:1, 2) with a strenuous but unsuccessful effort to bring back the ten tribes to their allegiance.

people.name: Ahaziah
people.summary: The son of Joram, or Jehoram, and sixth king of Judah. Called Jehoahaz (2 Chr. 21:17; 25:23), and Azariah (2 Chr. 22:6). Guided by his idolatrous mother Athaliah, his reign was disastrous (2 Kings 8:24-29; 9:29).

people.name: Joash
people.summary: The son of King Ahaziah. While yet an infant, he was saved from the general massacre of the family by his aunt Jehosheba, and was apparently the only surviving descendant of Solomon (2 Chr. 21:4, 17).

people.name: Jehoram
people.summary: The eldest son and successor of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah. He reigned eight years (B.C. 892-885) alone as king of Judah, having been previously for some years associated with his father (2 Chr. 21:5, 20; 2 Kings 8:16).

people.name: Amaziah
people.summary: The son and successor of Joash, and eighth king of the separate kingdom of Judah (2 Kings 14:1-4). He began his reign by punishing the murderers of his father (5-7; 2 Chr. 25:3-5).

people.name: Uzziah
people.summary: One of Amaziah’s sons, whom the people made king of Judah in his father’s stead (2 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 26:1). His long reign of about fifty-two years was “the most prosperous excepting that of Jehosaphat since the time of Solomon.”

people.name: Jotham
people.summary: The son and successor of Uzziah on the throne of Judah. As during his last years Uzziah was excluded from public life on account of his leprosy, his son, then twenty-five years of age, administered for seven years the affairs of the kingdom in his father’s stead (2 Chr. 26:21, 23; 27:1).

people.name: Hezekiah
people.summary: Son of Ahaz (2 Kings 18:1; 2 Chr. 29:1), whom he succeeded on the throne of the kingdom of Judah. He reigned twenty-nine years (B.C. 726-697).

people.name: Ahaz
people.summary: The son and successor of Jotham, king of Judah (2 Kings 16; Isa. 7-9; 2 Chr. 28). He gave himself up to a life of wickedness and idolatry. Notwithstanding the remonstrances and warnings of Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah, he appealed for help against Rezin, king of Damascus, and Pekah, king of Israel, who threatened Jerusalem, to Tiglath-pileser, the king of Assyria, to the great injury of his kingdom and his own humilating subjection to the Assyrians (2 Kings 16:7, 9; 15:29).

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

people.name: Josiah
people.summary: Healed by Jehovah, or Jehovah will support. The son of Amon, and his successor on the throne of Judah (2 Kings 22:1; 2 Chr. 34:1). His history is contained in 2 Kings 22, 23.

people.name: Amon
people.summary: The son of Manasseh, and fourteenth king of Judah. He restored idolatry, and set up the images which his father had cast down.

people.name: Zedekiah
people.summary: The last king of Judah. He was the third son of Josiah, and his mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, and hence he was the brother of Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:31; 24:17, 18).

people.name: Jehoiakim
people.summary: He whom Jehovah has set up, the second son of Josiah, and eighteenth king of Judah, which he ruled over for eleven years (B.C. 610-599).

people.name: Jehoahaz
people.summary: A son of king Josiah (1 Chr. 3:15; Jer. 22:11), who was elected to succeed his father on the throne, although he was two years younger than his brother Eliakim.

people.name: Johanan
people.summary: The oldest of King Josiah’s sons (1 Chr. 3:15).

people.name: Jehoiachin
people.summary: Succeeded his father Jehoiakin (B.C. 599) when only eight years of age, and reigned for one hundred days (2 Chr. 36:9). He is also called Jeconiah (Jer. 24:1; 27:20, etc.), and Coniah (22:24; 37:1).

people.name: Zedekiah
people.summary: Jehoiachin.

people.name: Shealtiel
people.summary: Asked for of God, father of Zerubbabel (Ezra 3:2, 8; Neh. 12:1).

people.name: Pedaiah
people.summary: The father of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:17-19).

people.name: Nedabiah
people.summary: Moved of Jehovah, one of the sons of Jeconiah (1 Chr. 3:18).

people.name: Zerubbabel
people.summary: The seed of Babylon, the son of Salathiel or Shealtiel (Hag. 1:1; Zorobabel, Matt. 1:12); called also the son of Pedaiah (1 Chr. 3:17-19), i.e., according to a frequent usage of the word “son;” the grandson or the nephew of Salathiel.

people.name: Hananiah
people.summary: Son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:19, 21).

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: A son of Pedaiah, the brother of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:19).

people.name: Berechiah
people.summary: The fourth of the five sons of Zerubbabel, of the royal family of Judah (1 Chr. 3:20).

people.name: Hasadiah
people.summary: Favoured by Jehovah, one of the sons of Pedaiah (1 Chr. 3:20), of the royal line of David.

people.name: Hashubah
people.summary: Ibid., a descendant of David (1 Chr. 3:20).

people.name: Ohel
people.summary: A house; tent, the fourth son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:20).

people.name: Shechaniah
people.summary: A priest whose sons are mentioned in 1 Chr. 3:21, 22.

people.name: Jesaiah
people.summary: One of the three sons of Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:21).

people.name: Pelatiah
people.summary: A son of Hananiah and grandson of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:21).

people.name: Rephaiah
people.summary: Son of David.

people.name: Neariah
people.summary: Sons: Hattush.

people.name: Bariah
people.summary: Fugitive, one of Shemaiah’s five sons.

people.name: Shaphat
people.summary: Son of Shemaiah.

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: A False Prophet.

people.name: Azrikam
people.summary: Son of Neariah.

people.name: Hezekiah
people.summary: King of Judah.

people.name: Akkub
people.summary: A descendant of David (1 Chr. 3:24).

people.name: Johanan
people.summary: Son of Neariah.

people.name: Pelaiah
people.summary: One of David’s posterity (1 Chr. 3:24).

places.name: Hebron
places.summary: A city in the south end of the valley of Eshcol, about midway between Jerusalem and Beersheba, from which it is distant about 20 miles in a straight line.

places.name: Geshur
places.summary: Bridge, the name of a district or principality of Syria near Gilead, between Mount Hermon and the Lake of Tiberias (2 Sam. 15:8; 1 Chr. 2:23).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).
